authorization: Owner approvals cmsg_01Gr5R4j3t2Yet65UcmhcVhADwvzg9kA9GinuWu3D7FSfe and cmsg_01Gr5R4j3t2Yet65UcmhcVhAAAbp6kqDfMqxzNm3PL6f5g (standing approvals, applied 2026-11-23): «Objetos perdidos» (ID 264), a new A0–C2 3D conversation and listening class on the night shift at a municipal lost-and-found office, whose A0 level is fully bilingual (conversation, extras, choices, ledger and listening) and whose A1 level glosses its key words in English, plus one English line for the academies listing. This manifest approves only the exact English literals listed below; it cannot exempt any edit or deletion of existing English copy.

additions.text: The night shift at a lost-and-found office in 3D: absurd claims, small mysteries and owners to reunite with their things, all in Spanish.
Don Evaristo comes to the counter. He talks to Don Celestino.
Good evening, sir. What are you looking for?
My false teeth. They fell out last night at the festival. Dancing.
Here is a box with three sets of false teeth.
Three! And which one is mine?
I don’t know. One was inside a tuba.
What is Don Evaristo looking for?
Where did he lose his false teeth?
How many sets of false teeth are in the box?
Where was one set of false teeth?
What do you lose often?
What music do you dance to at a party?
Where do you leave your things at night?
false teeth
dancing
box
Rocío comes to the office with something in her hand.
Hello. This umbrella is not mine.
Whose is it?
A guy’s from the festival. It was raining and he gave it to me.
Look, it says something inside: “If you find me, call Teo.”
Teo! His name is Teo.
What does Rocío bring?
Whose is the umbrella?
What was the weather like at the festival?
What is the guy’s name?
What do you do when it rains and you have no umbrella?
What do you lend a stranger?
What colour is your umbrella?
umbrella
it was raining
guy

I am a locksmith. I open all the doors in the city.

How does Wilson feel?

workshop

Good evening, Celestino. And my glove?
Good evening, Aurora. A red glove, from 1986?
Yes. I lost it at the lantern festival. Forty years ago.
Well… here it is. It’s in my drawer.
What colour is the glove?
What year is the glove from?

My wedding is on Saturday and I don’t have the ring.

The thing is… the ring has a name on it. And it isn’t your name.

This canoe is mine. It’s called La Gaviota.

I’m looking for a small box. It’s my dog Canelo’s ashes.

Canelo looks after the bus. Like he looks after my house.

Last night, at the festival, I let go of a paper lantern with a wish.

I have number 247. It’s urgent! I am the mayor’s secretary.
What are you looking for?

Ah, yes. But it isn’t gold. It’s chocolate.

Neighbour with ticket 112, waiting since nine
I have ticket 112. I have been waiting since nine. I am looking for my glasses, but without glasses I can’t see the screen.
What thing do you always look for at home?
Festival dancer who lost his shoes
I danced all night. Now I don’t have shoes. They are red, patent leather. My feet are very tired.
What shoes do you wear for a party?
Student who lost her backpack with her notes
I lost my backpack at the festival. My notes are inside. Tomorrow I have a history exam.
How do you study for a difficult exam?
Neighbour dressed as a giant lantern
I am a lantern. It is my costume. I am looking for the costume’s head. Without the head, I am a sad lamp.
What costume would you like to wear at a party?
Town street sweeper who brings what she finds in the street
I clean the street after the festival. I find everything: shoes, keys, a violin. I bring it here.
What curious thing did you ever find in the street?
Bike courier who lost a delivery
I am a delivery rider. I lost a pizza at the festival. The customer has been waiting for three hours. Poor customer.
What food do you order for delivery when you are at home?
Volunteer charging the sixty-four phones
I charge the lost phones. There are sixty-four. When one rings, I answer: “Lost and found, how can I help?”
Where do you leave your phone when you dance at a party?
The office’s maintenance man for thirty years
I fix the lights and doors of the office. Tonight the ticket machine is broken. Again.
Which machine in your home makes strange noises?
Clerk who sorts odd gloves
I sort gloves. I have three hundred gloves and no complete pair. It is a strange job, but I like it.
What clothes do you lose most often?
Intern in his first week, freezing cold
I am the intern. I work in the cold room. It is very cold here. I am wearing two jumpers and a hat.
What do you wear for a street party night?
Retired archivist who comes to read the old ledgers
I worked here for thirty years. Now I come to read the old books. I like them more than novels.
What book or magazine are you reading now?
Musician in the town band, the bass drummer
I play the bass drum in the band. Fidel is my bandmate. Last night the tuba sounded very strange and very beautiful.
What instrument would you like to play?
Mother of the bride, looking for the ring harder than anyone
I am Vanesa’s mother. The wedding is on Saturday. We need the ring! I am not sleeping tonight.
What wedding or family celebration do you remember well?
Bus mechanic checking the number 14 bus
I am a mechanic. I am checking the number 14 bus. There is confetti in the engine. A lot of confetti.
What transport do you use to go to work or class?
Taxi driver, Rubén’s colleague at the harbour rank
I am a taxi driver, like Rubén. My car is yellow. Tonight I drove forty people. Forty!
Where do you go by taxi?
The festival DJ, resting on the rooftop
I am the festival DJ. I lost my headphones. Now I listen to the city. It is very quiet from here.
What music do you listen to at night?
Local newspaper photographer, with a flat camera battery
I am a photographer. I take photos of the festival for the newspaper. My camera has no battery. What bad luck!
What old photo do you keep on your phone?
A smile in a tuba
It is eleven at night. It is your first day at the lost-and-found office. At the counter there is an old man. He has no teeth.
Good evening. My name is Evaristo. I am looking for my false teeth.
There are three sets of teeth in the box. And there is a tuba with something inside.
My teeth are small and very nice!
Evaristo looks at you. What do you say?
Here are three sets of teeth. Which one is yours?
Not this one. Not this one… This one! It is in the tuba.
Evaristo smiles with his teeth. Celestino writes in the book.
You are cold. Here is a hot soup.
Thank you. I come back at seven, OK?
Evaristo drinks the soup without teeth. He is slow, but he is happy.
One moment. I call the music band.
The band? My teeth are music!
A musician brings the tuba. The teeth go back into Evaristo's mouth.
Who in your family has a nice smile?
What music plays at the festivals in your neighborhood?
What soup do you like in winter?
What time do you have dinner on Fridays?
Who smiles a lot in your family?

the tuba

Teo's umbrella
On the shelves there are many black umbrellas. A girl has an umbrella in her hand. It is not her umbrella.
Hi. My name is Rocío. This umbrella belongs to a boy. His name is Teo.
Look at the label: “If you find me, call Teo.”
Teo is very nice. And very handsome.
Rocío is nervous. What do you do?
There is a number on the label. Shall we call Teo?
Now? Well… yes. You call!
Teo answers. Rocío gives him the umbrella and her phone number.
Tomorrow it rains. Do you keep the umbrella?
Yes! It is a very good umbrella.
Rocío leaves with Teo's umbrella. Outside it is not raining.
I put it here, with the other umbrellas.
OK… There are a lot of black umbrellas, right?
Teo's umbrella is on the shelf, among more than a thousand black umbrellas.
Where do you leave your umbrella when you get home?
Do you have an umbrella in your backpack today?
What do you do at home on rainy days?
What name do you like for a boy?
Do you write your name on your things?

the label
the shelf

Three thousand keys
In the keys aisle there are three thousand keys. A man is looking for a small grey key.
I am Wilson. I am a locksmith. I open doors every day.
But today I don't have the key to my workshop. How embarrassing!
It is a grey key, with a red ribbon.
Wilson is sad. What do you say?
Let's look. Is it this one? And this one?
No… no… Yes! Number two thousand eight hundred seventy-one.
Wilson has his key. He celebrates with a little dance.
Here is a hairpin. You are a locksmith, right?
Of course! With a hairpin I open any door.
Wilson opens his workshop with a hairpin. He is a very good locksmith.
It is very late. There is a sofa in the waiting room.
A sofa… Yes, I am very tired.
Wilson sleeps on the sofa. Tomorrow he opens his workshop.
Which key do you use every day?
Where do you put your keys when you get home?
Who opens the door of your home in the morning?
Do you have a comfortable sofa at home?
What colour is your front door?

the workshop

Julio's voice
In the phone room there are sixty-four phones. One phone rings and rings. An old lady is waiting.
I am Herminia. I am eighty-one years old. I am looking for my phone.
On my phone there is the voice of Julio, my husband. Julio is dead.
My phone is old and blue.
Herminia has sad eyes. What do you do?
Here is a blue phone with no battery. I have an old charger.
It is my phone! Does it work?
The phone works. Herminia hears Julio's voice and smiles.
Listen. A phone is ringing a lot. Is it yours?
Yes! It is Iker, my grandson. He calls all night.
Herminia answers. Her grandson is very happy.
Here it is. We save Julio's voice on the computer.
On the computer? How modern!
Now Julio's voice is in three places. Herminia is calm.
What colour is your phone?
Who do you call on the phone every week?
What voice message do you keep on your phone?
Who do you call to share good news?
Do you have old photos at home?
the phone
the charger
the voice
the grandson
A very old tree
In the cold room there are plants and food. It is very cold. A man is looking at a small tree.
I am Gaspar. This bonsai is my grandfather's. It is sixty years old.
I water the bonsai every day. Twenty years.
But… it is strange. The leaves are not normal.
You touch the bonsai. It is plastic. What do you say?
It is your bonsai. It is plastic, but it is your grandfather's.
Plastic… Well. It is my bonsai.
Gaspar carries the bonsai in his arms, like a baby.
Gaspar, the bonsai is plastic. Twenty years of water!
Plastic? Oh, grandpa! It is a joke!
Gaspar laughs a lot. It is the first time since the funeral.
It is cold here. Shall we come back tomorrow?
Yes, better tomorrow. I don't want to know more.
The bonsai is in the cold room. Gaspar doesn't know the truth.
How many plants are there in your kitchen?
What thing of your grandmother or grandfather do you like?
What do you do every day in the morning?
Do you like jokes?
What plant do you have in the window?
the bonsai
the plastic

Mum's lentils
In the cold room there are two hundred and twelve plastic containers. A man is looking for his mother's container.
Hi. I am Álex. My mother's name is Lupe.
The container has her name on it. Inside there are lentils.
My mother cooks very well. I don't.
Álex looks at the containers. What do you do?
This container says “Lupe”. It is your mother's!
Yes! Thank you. I am calling my mother right now.
It is four in the morning. His mother answers very happily.
Look. There is a note inside.
The note says: “Call me more.” Oh, mum…
Álex promises to call his mother every Sunday.
Here is a red container. Does this one do?
It is similar… Yes, it does.
Álex takes another container. His mother is going to notice.
Who makes the lentils in your family?
What food of your mother or father do you like?
Do you like lentils?
What food does someone at home make for you?
What food do you take to work or class?

the lentils
the note

A red glove
The archive has forty old books. An old lady is looking for a red glove. She comes every year.
I am Aurora. I am looking for a red glove. It is from nineteen eighty-six.
Madam, there is no glove. I am sorry.
Celestino, every year you say the same thing.
Celestino has his hand in a drawer. What do you do?
Here, in the first book, it says: “red glove”.
My glove! After forty years!
Aurora has her red glove on her hand. Celestino is red too.
Celestino, what is in your drawer?
A red glove… for forty years.
Celestino gives the glove to Aurora. They are both silent.
It is late. Do you look for the glove together next year?
Together? Well… yes, I like the idea.
Aurora and Celestino have a date: next year, here.
Do you wear gloves in the winter in your city?
What do you keep in a drawer at home?
What year is special for your family?
What place do you visit every year?
Who do you dance with at a party?

the drawer
the book
The name in the ring
In the room of big objects there is a wedding dress and a canoe. A bride and her groom are looking for a ring.
I am Vanesa. I am getting married on Saturday. We don't have the ring!
Well… the ring has a problem.
A problem? What problem, Óliver?
Óliver is nervous. What do you do?
Look, the ring is in the pocket of the dress.
Here it is! But… it says “Jessica”. Who is Jessica?
Óliver explains everything. Vanesa now knows who Jessica is.
A tin ring is cheap and pretty.
Tin? Well… for Saturday, OK.
The ring with the name “Jessica” is at the office. On Saturday there is a tin ring.
What if we write “Jessica no” on the ring?
“Jessica no”… I like it! It is funny.
Vanesa takes the ring. Tomorrow they go to the jeweller.
What jewellery do you like to give as a gift?
What clothes do you wear for a wedding?
What day of the week is good for a wedding?
What is your cousin's name?
Do you have many pockets in your clothes today?

Fidel's tuba
In the room of big objects there is a huge tuba. A musician from the band is waiting next to it.
I am Fidel. I play the tuba in the city band.
Last night my tuba sounded very good. Very, very good!
But inside the tuba there is a set of false teeth.
Fidel looks at his tuba. What do you say?

Thank you. My normal tuba… it's fine.

The tuba stays at the office for a week. You practise without the teeth.
A week? Phew… OK.
The tuba is at the office. Fidel practises at home with a flute.
Fidel, the tuba sounds good because you play well.
Me? Really?
Fidel plays the tuba in the room. It sounds very nice. Without teeth.
Do you like band music?
What instrument is there in your home?
What song do you like a lot?
What thing do you do better without an audience?
What music is there at your neighbourhood parties?
the band
the musician
to play
A canoe for two
In the room there is an old canoe. It is called La Gaviota. Two men want the canoe.
I am Nacho. The canoe is mine.
No. I am Guille, and the canoe is mine.
Guille and I don't talk. Ten years without talking.
They are both angry. What do you do?
The canoe is big. Do you both carry it?
Together? Well… it is heavy.
Nacho and Guille carry La Gaviota. One in front and one behind.
The canoe stays here until tomorrow. You talk.
Talk? No. Better not.
The canoe stays at the office. Nacho and Guille leave through different doors.
Look. Here there are two names: Nacho and Guille.
Our names… from nineteen ninety-eight.
Nacho and Guille read the names. After ten years, there is a hug.
Do you like water or do you prefer mountains?
How old is your best friendship?
Do you like rowing on a lake?
Where is there water to swim in your city?
What thing do you share with your family?
the canoe
the name
the hug
heavy
Canelo on the bus
On the loading dock there is a bus. It is line fourteen. A man is looking for a small box.
I am Lisandro. In the box are the ashes of Canelo, my dog.
I am Mari Carmen, the driver. The box is here, on my bus!
Canelo travelled with me all night.
Lisandro cries a little. What do you say?
Here is Canelo. Now he goes home.
Thank you. My wife is waiting.
Lisandro takes the box home. Canelo is with his family.
One last ride on the bus, with Canelo?
Yes. Canelo really likes the bus.
Lisandro and Canelo do one last ride. Then, home.
Mari Carmen, a photo of Canelo on the bus?
Yes! A photo next to the steering wheel.
Now Canelo always travels on line fourteen, in a photo.
What animal lives on your street?
Do you sleep on the bus or on the train?
What number is your bus?

What photo do you have on your phone?
the bus
the ashes
the driver
the dog
A parrot with two homes
On the dock there is a taxi. Next to it there is a green parrot in a cage. A man and a lady are arguing.
I am Rubén. I am a taxi driver. This parrot is mine! His name is Fígaro.
I am Fefa. Fígaro lives in my house. Six years.
Fígaro, say “Rubén”!
The parrot looks at both. What do you say?
Fígaro says “Rubén”. He belongs to Rubén.
Fígaro! My friend!
Fígaro goes back with Rubén. Fefa waves goodbye.
Fígaro lives with Fefa. Rubén visits on Sundays.
On Sundays… with coffee, OK?
Fígaro has two homes and two friends.
Fígaro stays at the office until tomorrow.
At the office? Poor Fígaro!
The parrot stays at the office. He repeats words from Rubén and Fefa.
What animal does someone in your family have?
What bird do you see from your home?
Who do you visit on Sundays?
Do you use taxis a lot?
What phrase of your mother's do you repeat a lot?

the cage
the taxi
to repeat
Fourteen wallets
In the street there is a man with a bag. Inside there are fourteen wallets.
Hi. I am Tato. I bring fourteen wallets from the festival.
They are not mine. I am… well… a thief. A retired thief.
Is there a reward? Ten percent, please.
Tato waits. What do you say?
There is no reward. But here is a receipt.
A receipt? Well… it is my first receipt.
Tato leaves with a receipt. He is happy.
Thank you, Tato. Are you looking for work?
Work? Yes! Here, at the office?
The wallets go back to their owners. Tato waits for the boss.
Ten percent is not possible.
No? Then goodbye. And the wallets come with me.
Tato leaves with the fourteen wallets. What a problem!
What do you carry in your wallet?
What colour is your bag or backpack?
What do you do with money you find in the street?
Are there many people in your street at night?
What job is good for a very fast person?
the wallet
the thief
the receipt
the reward
A boy in pyjamas
In front of the pharmacy there is a bench. On the bench there is a young man in pyjamas. He has one shoe.
Where am I? I am Benja. I don't know anything.
I am Gloria, the pharmacist. You are in the street, in pyjamas.
And you have a trophy. It is from karaoke.
Benja looks at the trophy. What do you say?
At the office there is a shoe and a phone. Are they yours?
My shoe! My phone! And the trophy?
Benja has his shoe, his phone and a new trophy.
Benja, last night you sang at the party. You are the karaoke king!
Me? Sing? How embarrassing!
